entity_texture_features.config.entity_texture_features.property_:
Hardcore
If the world is hardcore mode or not
§ahardcore.<n>=<true/false>

List of biomes
The vanilla biome names are listed here: https://minecraft.gamepedia.com/Biome#Biome_IDs
Biomes added by mods can also be used but require "modID:biomeName", whereas vanilla biomes can be either "minecraft:plains" or just "plains".
With ETF only, you can also use regex: iregex: pattern: and ipattern: like the Name property
§abiomes.<n>=<biome_list>

List of game modes of the client player
In vanilla these are: 0=survival, 1=creative, 2=adventure, 3=spectator
§aclientGameMode.<n>=<list>

List of difficulties
Vanilla difficulties are: 0=peaceful, 1=easy, 2=normal, 3=hard
§adifficulty.<n>=<list>

List of regional difficulties
 ranges between 0.0 to 6.75 different per chunk
 see https://minecraft.wiki/w/Difficulty#Regional_difficulty
§aregionalDifficulty.<n>=<list>

Blocks
sets the texture for the entity based on the block it is on
this also checks the block it is inside allowing things like water, cave_air, flowers, etc. to be used
Blocks added by mods can also be used but require "modID:blockName", whereas vanilla blocks can be either "minecraft:stone" or just "stone".
as of v4.4 this property also allows comparing additional block properties as per the OptiFine spec here https://optifine.readthedocs.io/syntax.html#blocks-and-items
§ablocks.<n>=<block_list>

Blocks spawned
sets the texture for the entity based on the block it spawned on or first appeared on
this also checks the block it spawned inside allowing things like water, cave_air, flowers, etc. to be used
Blocks added by mods can also be used but require "modID:blockName", whereas vanilla blocks can be either "minecraft:stone" or just "stone".
as of v4.4 this property also allows comparing additional block properties as per the OptiFine spec here https://optifine.readthedocs.io/syntax.html#blocks-and-items
§ablockSpawned.<n>=<block_list>

Height ranges
Replaces legacy minHeight and maxHeight properties.
Since 1.18 negative values may be specified for height. When used in a range they can be put in brackets for Optifine but will function as written for ETF.
ETF supports:             1 2-4   -65-2  -65--2   1-4   (-65)-2  (-65)-(-2)
Optifine supports only:   1 2-4                   1-4   (-65)-2  (-65)-(-2)
§aheights.<n>=<height_ranges>

Height legacy
ETF also supports the legacy minHeight and maxHeight properties.
they can be a single number from -64 to 319
§aminHeight.<n>=<height>
§amaxHeight.<n>=<height>

Name
Matches to an entities name.
A value starting with "!" performs a negative match (not).
Examples:
 - Match string: "name=Pinky pinkyyy"
 - Match special formatting: "name=\u00a74\u00a7oPinky"
   (for best compatibility, use the escape sequence '\u00a7' instead of "§")
 - Wildcards using "?" and "*": "name=pattern:Pinky*"
 - Wildcards, case insensitive: "name=ipattern:Pinky*"
 - Java regular expressions: "name=regex:Pin(k)+y"
   (see http://docs.oracle.com/javase/6/docs/api/java/util/regex/Pattern.html)
 - Java regular expressions, case insensitive: "name=iregex:Pin(k)+y"
Any backslashes in the match string must be doubled.
Literal backslashes within a regular expression or wildcard must be quadrupled.
Correct:
  name=regex:\\d+
  name=regex:\\\\
  name=/\\/\\
Wrong:
  name=regex:\d+
  name=regex:\\
  name=/\/\
§anames.<n>=<name_list|regex|pattern>

Teams
ETF only!
This is identical to the Names property behaviour however allows definition by way of scoreboard teams
supports grouping names between "" quotations.
you can also use regex: iregex: pattern: and ipattern: like the Name property
Example:
 - teams.1=Red red red_team "red team"
§ateams.<n>=<teams>

Professions 
List of villager professions with levels
Entry format
  <profession>[:level1,level2,...]
Professions: none, armorer, butcher, cartographer, cleric, farmer, fisherman, fletcher,
             leatherworker, librarian, mason, nitwit, shepherd, toolsmith, weaponsmith
Example:
Professions farmer (all levels) or librarian (levels 1,3,4)
  professions=farmer librarian:1,3-4
  professions=minecraft:farmer minecraft:librarian:1,3-4
Professions full
  professions=fisherman shepherd minecraft:nitwit villager_mod:town_mayor
  professions=minecraft:fisherman minecraft:shepherd minecraft:nitwit
§aprofessions.<n>=<professions>

Colors 
List of wolf/cat collar colors or sheep/llama colors
ETF also supports shulker colors & tropical fish colours (but only for the base fish texture)
Colors: white orange magenta light_blue yellow lime pink gray light_gray cyan purple blue brown green red black
Example:
  colors.2=pink magenta purple
The legacy property "collarColors" is also recognized
§acolors.<n>=<colors>

Baby 
Only valid for mobs
§ababy.<n>=<true/false>

Health 
Range of health values, can also be given in percent.
Only valid for mobs.
Example:
  health.1=10
  health.2=5-8 10-12
  health.3=0-50%
§ahealth.<n>=<list>

Moon phase 
List of moon phases (0-7)
Example
  moonPhase.1=3
  moonPhase.2=0 1 2
  moonPhase.1=0-2 4-7
§amoonPhase.<n>=<list>

Day time 
List of day times in ticks (0-24000)
Example
  dayTime.1=2000-10000
  dayTime.2=0-1000 18000-24000
§adayTime.<n>=<list>

Weather 
Several values can be specified, separated by space
for example "weather=clear rain thunder"
§aweather.<n>=<clear|rain|thunder>

Sizes 
Only valid for mobs with multiple sizes (0-255 for slimes and magma cubes and 0-64 for phantoms)
Slimes and magma cubes naturally spawn in three sizes: 0=small, 1=medium, 3=big.
Naturally spawning phantoms only spawn in one size: 0.
Example
  sizes.1=3
  sizes.2=0 1 3
  sizes.3=0-2 4-7
§asizes.<n>=<list>

NBT 
Select whether a mob must have matching NBT data values
Note: this is an OptiFine feature that has not yet received official documentation,
ETF has copied the syntax listed in https://optifine.readthedocs.io/syntax.html#nbt for now.
NBT requires an additional value in the key this is called <nbtPath>.
- nbtPath must match the exact name of the nbt element and is case-sensitive
- nbtPath supports matching nested nbt elements by defining the full nbt path with '.' marking a separation
- E.G. the Villager profession level nbtPath is "VillagerData.level" meaning the full property key would be "nbt.<n>.VillagerData.level"
NBT can be used in several ways see this link https://optifine.readthedocs.io/syntax.html#nbt for details
Additionally ETF adds a variation to the "raw:" syntax called "print_raw:" which will act just like "raw:" but will
also print what that raw value is to the log for testing purposes,
ETF also allows you to start the string with "print:" to always print the full NBT data of the entity
§anbt.<n>.<nbtPath>=<exists:|raw:|print_raw:|print:|range:|regex:|iregex:|pattern:|ipattern:|string_list>

NBT Vehicle 
Select whether a mob's ridden entity must have matching NBT data values
Works exactly like the NBT property but for the ridden entity, false if it doesn't exist
§anbtVehicle.<n>.<nbtPath>=<exists:|raw:|print_raw:|print:|range:|regex:|iregex:|pattern:|ipattern:|string_list>

NBT Client 
Select whether the client player must have matching NBT data values
Works exactly like the NBT property but for the client players nbt
§anbtClient.<n>.<nbtPath>=<exists:|raw:|print_raw:|print:|range:|regex:|iregex:|pattern:|ipattern:|string_list>

Speed Ranges 
ETF Only!
Select a range of top speeds a mob must match
Functional for all mobs but intended for Horses, Donkeys & Mules
Horse, Donkey & Mule speeds exist within a range of: 0.1125 - 0.3375
The "-" and two numbers either side are necessary
§aspeed.<n>=minimum_speed - maximum_speed

Jump Strength 
ETF Only!
Select a range of Jump Strength a mob must match
Functional for Horses, Donkeys & Mules
Horse, Donkey & Mule jump strengths exist within a range of: 0.4 - 1.0
The "-" and two numbers either side are necessary
§ajumpStrength.<n>=minimum_strength - maximum_strength

Max Health 
ETF Only!
Select Max Health values a mob must match
Functional for all mobs but intended for Horses, Donkeys & Mules
Horse, Donkey & Mule max health exist within a range of: 15 - 30
Example: maxHealth.1= 3 5 15-20 25 27-29
§amaxHealth.<n>=<list>

Llama Inventory Slots 
ETF Only!
Select Inventory size values a llama must match
Functional for Llamas only
Llama inventory sizes exist within a range of: 1 - 5
Example: llamaInventory.1= 1 4-5
§allamaInventory.<n>=<list>

Panda Hidden Gene 
ETF Only!
Select what hidden gene a panda must have
§ahiddenGene.<n>=<normal|lazy|worried|playful|brown|weak|aggressive>

Player Created Golem 
ETF Only!
Select whether an Iron Golem must be player created or naturally spawned
true = player made, false = naturally spawned
§aplayerCreated.<n>=<true|false>

Screaming Goats 
ETF Only!
Select whether a Goat needs to be the screaming variant or not
true = must be screaming goat, false = must be normal goat
§ascreamingGoat.<n>=<true|false>

Distance from player 
ETF Only!
Select what distance from the Player a mob must match
Values are in blocks, ranges can be used like: 1-5
Example: distanceFromPlayer.1= 3 5 15-20 25 27-50
§adistance.<n>=<list>

Charged Creeper 
ETF Only!
Select whether a Creeper needs to be charged by lightning or not
true = charged, false = normal
§acreeperCharged.<n>=<true|false>

Angry 
ETF Only!
Select whether a Mob must be in their angered / attacking state or not
works for Endermen, Blazes, Guardians, Vindicators and Evokers
Triggers when these mobs display their client side 'angered or attacking state' (e.g. open mouth for endermen & blazes igniting)
Example: angry.1=true
§aangry.<n>=<true|false>

Items 
Select whether a mob must have certain, or any, items equipped or held
Example: items.1=minecraft:book cool_mod:sunglasses   (matches a mob holding or wearing one of these items)
Example: items.1=any                                  (matches a mob holding or wearing any item)
Example: items.1=wearing                              (matches a mob wearing any item)
Example: items.1=none                                 (matches a mob holding or wearing no items)
§aitems.<n>=<list|none|any|holding|wearing>

Moving 
Select whether a mob must be moving or standing still
Note: functionally this only detects horizontal movement as vertical velocity is quite unstable in the code
Example: moving.1=false   (matches only a mob standing still)
§amoving.<n>=<true|false>

Spawner 
ETF Only!
Select whether a mob must be a miniature mob inside a mob spawner block
Example: isSpawner.1=true
§aisSpawner.<n>=<true|false>

Dimension 
ETF Only!
Select which dimension a mob must be in
Can prefix with "print:" to always print the dimension the mob is in to the log
helps to identify modded dimension names
Example: dimension.1=minecraft:overworld
§adimension.<n>=<overworld|the_nether|the_end|<modded_dimension_name>>

Light 
ETF Only!
Select which light level a mob must be in from 0-15
Example: light.1=0-7 9 14
§alight.<n>=<list>

Variant 
ETF Only!
Select which variant a mob must be
This property will work with any vanilla or modded entity that implements the VariantHolder class and
will use the string representation of the type, e.g. "black" for a cat, "oak" for a boat.
This property also works uniquely with these block entities:
- signs (wood)
- bed (color)
- shulkerbox (color)
- Decorated pot (all 4 sherd face types)
- skulls(appending facing direction at the end)
For all other regular & block entities it returns the EntityType or BlockEntityType registry id.
This allows for the separation of different entity types that might use the same model or texture.
Can prefix with "print:" to always print the variant the mob appears as to the log
Example: variant.1=black yellow
§avariant.<n>=<list>

Creative 
ETF Only!
Select whether a player must be in creative mode or not
true = creative mode, false = survival mode
§aisCreative.<n>=<true|false>

Teammate 
ETF Only!
Select whether a mob must be a teammate of the player
true = teammate, false = not a teammate
§aisTeammate.<n>=<true|false>

Client Player 
ETF Only!
Select whether a mob must be the client player
true = client player, false = not the client player
§aisClientPlayer.<n>=<true|false>

Language 
Select which language the game must be set to
Example: language.1=en_us
§alanguage.<n>=<language_code>

Hour 
Select which hour of the day it must be in 24 hour format from 0 - 23
Example: hour.1=0-6 18-23
§ahour.<n>=<list>

Minute 
Select which minute of the hour it must be from 0 - 59
Example: minute.1=0-30
§aminute.<n>=<list>

Second 
Select which second of the minute it must be from 0 - 59
Example: second.1=0-30
§asecond.<n>=<list>

Month 
Select which month of the year it must be from 0 - 11
Example: month.1=1-6
§amonth.<n>=<list>

Year 
Select which year it must be from 0 - 9999
Example: year.1=2020-2022
§ayear.<n>=<list>

Biome Tag 
Select which Biome Tags the entities spawn biome can have
Example: biomeTag.1=is_river magic_mod:magical_biomes
§abiomeTag.<n>=<list>

Temperature 
Select what temperature it must be at the entities spawn location, this is internally driven by Biome settings as well as world height, for example if the biome has precipitation it will snow if the position is below 0.15 temperature
Example: temperature.1=0.2-0.15
§atemperature.<n>=<list>

Minecraft Version 
Select which minecraft version it must be
Example: minecraftVersion.1=1.18.2 1.17 1.20-1.99
§aminecraftVersion.<n>=<list>

Week day 
Select which day of the week it must be from 1 - 7 with 1 being Sunday and 7 being Saturday
Example: weekDay.1=1-4
§aweekDay.<n>=<list>

Month Day 
Select which day of the month it must be from 1 - 31
Example: monthDay.1=1-15
§amonthDay.<n>=<list>

Year Day 
Select which day of the year it must be from 1 - 366
Example: yearDay.1=1-100
§ayearDay.<n>=<list>

Block Above 
Vary based on the first non-air block above the entity, no matter the distance
Example: blockAbove.1=oak_leaves
§ablockAbove.<n>=<list>

Block Above Solid 
Vary based on the first solid non-air block above the entity, no matter the distance, only triggers for the first solid block found.
Example: blockAboveSolid.1=stone
§ablockAboveSolid.<n>=<list>

Block Below 
Vary based on the first non-air block below the entity, no matter the distance
Example: blockBelow.1=oak_leaves
§ablockBelow.<n>=<list>

Block Below Solid 
Vary based on the first solid non-air block below the entity, no matter the distance, only triggers for the first solid block found.
Example: blockBelowSolid.1=oak_leaves
§ablockBelowSolid.<n>=<list>

Mods Loaded 
Select what mods must be loaded
for instance if you need to disable or modify certain textures or animations for certain mod compatibilites
Example: modLoaded.1=sodium iris
§amodLoaded.<n>=<list>

Texture Rule (Optional)
matches the last random texture rule number that the entities texture matched against
defaults to 0

§atextureRule.<n>=<list>

Texture Suffix (Optional)

defaults to 0

fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.blocks.add.delay.desc:
Adds a Delay Gate block. On the first reach, it starts a one-time timer and skips its contained actions. The surrounding script continues immediately.

This block does not schedule an execution. Its timer is checked only when the script reaches the same block instance again. Reaches before the timer expires skip the contained actions. The first reach at or after expiry opens the gate and runs them; every later reach runs them immediately.

Delay time is in milliseconds. A resolved delay of 0 or less, including invalid values, opens the gate immediately.

The gate resets only when that action-script instance is reconstructed or replaced.

Use Execute Later instead when every reach should schedule a fresh delayed execution.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.blocks.add.execute_lat:
Adds an Execute Later block that schedules its contained actions to run after the specified delay.

Delay time is in milliseconds.

Every time the script reaches this block, it schedules a new execution on the main thread.

This is useful for delayed actions in scripts that only run once.

fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.copy_file.desc:
This action copies a file or folder in the game directory, which starts at the root of the Minecraft instance directory. This action is limited to work only inside the game directory for safety reasons.

It is also possible to access the default '.minecraft' directory with this action. For that, just start paths with the '.minecraft/' prefix.

Append '*' to the end of the source path to copy every file directly inside that folder. This wildcard ignores sub-directories and requires the destination to be a directory.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.create_file.desc:
This action creates a new empty file in the game directory, which starts at the root of the Minecraft instance directory. The file will only be created if it doesn't already exist. This action is limited to work only inside the game directory for safety reasons.

It is also possible to access the default '.minecraft' directory with this action. For that, just start paths with the '.minecraft/' prefix.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.delete_file.desc:
This action deletes a file or folder in the game directory, which starts at the root of the Minecraft instance directory. This action is limited to work only inside the game directory for safety reasons.

It is also possible to access the default '.minecraft' directory with this action. For that, just start paths with the '.minecraft/' prefix.

Append '*' to the end of the target path to delete every file directly inside that folder. This wildcard ignores sub-directories and leaves the folder itself intact.

This action downloads a file from a URL and saves it to the game directory, which starts at the root of the Minecraft instance directory. This action is limited to work only inside the game directory for safety reasons.

Provide the download folder instead of a file name; FancyMenu derives the saved file name from the HTTP response headers or the URL automatically.

§lAsynchronous Download:§r This action downloads files asynchronously, which means the download happens in the background without freezing or blocking the game. The game will continue running normally while the file is being downloaded.

It is also possible to access the default '.minecraft' directory with this action. For that, just start paths with the '.minecraft/' prefix.

Opens a screen by its identifier.

Supports vanilla/mod screens and
custom GUIs made with FancyMenu.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.openlink.desc: Open a link in your default browser.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.paste_to_chat.append.d:
If the action should append the text to existing
text that is already typed in the input field.
The action will override existing text if this is disabled.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.paste_to_chat.desc: Paste text to the chat input field.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.play_audio.desc: Plays an audio resource once. Supports picking a sound channel and a base volume.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.play_audio.edit.audio_: The audio resource source to play. Supports resource locations, local files, web URLs and placeholders.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.play_audio.edit.base_v: A multiplier for the audio volume. 100% means full volume.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.play_audio.edit.choose: Opens a file chooser for FancyMenu audio resources.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.play_audio.edit.sound_: Which Minecraft sound category should be used for playback.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.play_audio.edit.title: Configure Play Audio
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.print_to_log.desc: This action will print text to the game's log/console for debugging.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.quitgame.desc: Stops the Minecraft client and begins its normal shutdown sequence.
Reloads resource packs, just like pressing F3 + T.

After a reload is triggered, this action has a five-second cooldown. Triggers during the cooldown are ignored.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.reloadmenu.desc:
Reloads FancyMenu, including stuff like
panoramas, slideshows, etc.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.rename_file.desc:
This action renames a file or folder in the game directory, which starts at the root of the Minecraft instance directory. This action is limited to work only inside the game directory for safety reasons.

It is also possible to access the default '.minecraft' directory with this action. For that, just start paths with the '.minecraft/' prefix.

Renaming a folder keeps its contents intact while updating its name.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.reset_element_animator: Resets the selected Element Animator and restarts its animation playback for all linked targets.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.screens.build_screen.e:
§zThis action has no value.
§zYou don't need to set one.
Edit the value of this action.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.screens.build_screen.f: §xYou need to edit the action value first!
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.screens.move_action_do:
Moves the selected entry down in the
list, so it gets executed later.
This is more precise than using
drag-&-drop to move entries.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.screens.move_action_up:
Moves the selected entry up in the
list, so it gets executed earlier.
This is more precise than using
drag-&-drop to move entries.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.script_editor.cancel_w:
Do you really want to §xcancel§r the script editing?
§xThis will undo everything you've done in here!
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.script_editor.empty_hi: Right-click here or press A to add actions
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.select_file.desc:
This action opens a native file selection dialog so you can pick a file from anywhere on your computer.
When a file is selected it gets copied to the configured target path inside the Minecraft instance directory (or the default '.minecraft' directory when the prefix is used).

FancyMenu also fires a listener with the selection result so you can trigger follow-up actions when the file was copied, the dialog was cancelled, or an error occurred.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.select_file.edit.exten:
Extensions that should be selectable in the file dialog.

Separate multiple entries with ',' or ';'.

Use values like 'png', 'jpg' or custom patterns such as '*.zip'.

Leave empty to allow every file.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.select_file.edit.filte:
The label shown in the native file dialog for the custom file filter.

Leave empty to use the default label.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.select_file.edit.overw: Choose whether FancyMenu should replace an existing file at the target path or cancel the action instead.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.select_file.edit.targe:
The destination that the selected file should be copied to.

Starts at the root of the Minecraft instance directory.

Use '.minecraft/' as prefix to target the default .minecraft directory.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.send_data_to_remote_se:
Connects to a remote WebSocket server (or reuses an existing connection) and sends text data.

FancyMenu automatically keeps one cached request ID per server URL and prefixes outgoing data with that request ID.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.send_fm_data_to_server:
Sends custom string data to the connected FancyMenu server using the FMData packet channel.
Use this together with '/fmdata listener ...' on the server to react to client-side events.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.send_http_request.desc:
Sends an HTTP request to a web target with configurable parameters.

This action allows you to send data to REST APIs, webhooks, or any HTTP endpoint.
Supports various authentication methods, custom headers, and different request types.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.send_http_request.edit:
The name of a FancyMenu variable the response should get written to.

§xIt's important to note that this action gets executed asynchronously,
§xso the variable value is not updated yet right after the action got executed.
Store Response as Single-Line in Variable: %s
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.sendmessage.desc: Send a chat message or command.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.set_text_input_field_v:
Sets the value of an input field (text box) by its element identifier.
Works for custom and Vanilla elements.
Does nothing if the element was not found or is not an input field.
The element identifier of the target element.
If enabled, the value will also be set when the input field is inactive.

The value that should be set on the target input field.
Placeholders are supported.
Configure Set Text Input Field Value Action
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.show_toast.desc: Displays a configurable toast notification. Supports custom width, icon, background texture, message and duration.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.show_toast.edit.choose: Toast backgrounds should be 32 pixels tall and match the toast width.
Toast icons look best at 20x20 pixels.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.show_toast.edit.clear_: Removes the custom background and falls back to Mojang's default toast sprite.
Removes the custom icon and uses an empty icon slot.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.show_toast.edit.durati: How long the toast remains visible. Measured in milliseconds.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.show_toast.edit.messag: Supports plain text (with § formatting codes) or a serialized JSON text component.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.show_toast.edit.title: Configure Toast
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.show_toast.edit.title_: Supports plain text (with § formatting codes) or a serialized JSON text component.
The toast width in pixels. The accepted range is 120–320 pixels, inclusive; values outside this range are clamped to the nearest limit. The default width is 160 pixels.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.spawn_element_instance:
Spawns a new element instance by deserializing an element body and injecting it into the active customization layer.
Spawned elements are not saved and disappear when the screen or layout reloads.

The serialized element body (single element container).
Paste the element block from a layout file if needed.
Placeholders are supported.

The identifier assigned to the spawned element.
Leave blank to auto-generate one.
Placeholders are supported.

The element type to spawn.
Changing this will reset the body to a default preset for the selected type.
No element types are currently available.
If disabled, placeholders inside the element body are not replaced before deserialization.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.start_scheduler.desc: Starts a scheduler by its unique identifier.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.stop_all_action_audios:
Stops all audios that are currently playing and were started via the "Play Audio" action.
This does not affect any other FancyMenu audio features such as button click sounds, Audio elements, menu open/close audios, etc.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.stop_scheduler.desc: Stops a scheduler by its unique identifier.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.toggle_element_animato: Toggles whether the Element Animator plays its animation for linked targets. The state persists across sessions.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.toggle_layout.desc: Toggle a layout (Enable/Disable) by its name.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.update_screen.desc:
Updates the current screen.
This is useful if you need to rebuild its
elements (like images, custom buttons, etc.),
or after changing the GUI scale or other
options that need the screen to get updated.
It's basically the same as resizing the window.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.variables.clearall.des: Clears ALL of FancyMenu's stored variables.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.variables.set.desc:
Store text content in a variable to use it
in placeholders, requirements and more.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.video.background.toggl:
Toggles the paused state of a Video menu background by its identifier.

To get the identifier of a background, right-click the
editor background and click on 'Copy Background Identifier'.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.video.set_video_backgr:
Seeks a Video menu background to a specific play time in milliseconds by its identifier.
The time is forced to be at least 0 and is not clamped to the video duration.

To get the identifier of a background, right-click the
editor background and click on 'Copy Background Identifier'.
Video Background Identifier + Play Time in Milliseconds [ Separated by : ]

Sets the volume of a Video menu background by its identifier.
The volume has to be a valid decimal between 0.0 (0%%) and 1.0 (100%%).

To get the identifier of a background, right-click the
editor background and click on 'Copy Background Identifier'.
Video Background Identifier + Volume [ Separated by : ]
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.video.set_video_elemen:
Seeks a Video element to a specific play time in milliseconds.
The time is forced to be at least 0 and is not clamped to the video duration.
Video Element Identifier + Play Time in Milliseconds [ Separated by : ]

Sets the volume of a Video element.
The volume has to be a valid decimal between 0.0 (0%%) and 1.0 (100%%).
Video Element Identifier + Volume [ Separated by : ]
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.video.toggle_paused_st: Toggles the paused state of a Video element.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.write_file.desc:
This action writes content to a file in the game directory, which starts at the root of the Minecraft instance directory. If the file doesn't exist, it will be created. This action is limited to work only inside the game directory for safety reasons.

It is also possible to access the default '.minecraft' directory with this action. For that, just start paths with the '.minecraft/' prefix.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.write_file.edit.conten:
The content to write to the file.
Use '\n' to represent line breaks. Click the edit button for multi-line editing.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.write_file.edit.mode.d: Choose whether to override the entire file content or append to the existing content.
fancymenu.fancymenu.actions.write_file.edit.target:
The path to the file to write to.
Starts at the root of the Minecraft instance directory.
Use '.minecraft/' prefix to access the default .minecraft directory.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.adaptive_continua:
Sets the minimum byte savings that an inter continuation should still provide before the encoder prefers a refresh.
Higher values force keyframes sooner, while lower values let longer dependency chains survive.
Enter a whole number greater than or equal to 0.

Sets the minimum relative savings ratio that an inter continuation should still provide.
This works together with the absolute byte threshold so large frames and small frames can be judged more fairly.
Enter a decimal value greater than or equal to 0.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.adaptive_keyframe:
Enables adaptive keyframe placement on top of the base keyframe interval.
When this is enabled, the planner can keep an inter chain alive longer if it is still saving space, or refresh earlier when the chain becomes expensive.
Disable it if you want stricter and more predictable full-frame placement.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.adaptive_max_keyf:
Sets the hard upper limit for adaptive keyframe spacing.
The encoder will never keep an inter chain alive longer than this value, even if it still compresses well.
Enter a whole number greater than 0.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.browse_intro_fram:
Opens a folder chooser for the optional intro animation.
Pick the directory that contains the ordered PNG files that should play once before the main loop starts.
Leave the intro empty if you do not need a separate intro sequence.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.browse_main_frame:
Opens a folder chooser for the main animation frames.
Pick the directory that contains the ordered PNG files for the main sequence.
The creator reads PNG files from that folder in natural filename order.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.browse_output.des:
Opens a save dialog for the exported AFMA file.
Choose the target folder and file name for the finished animation archive.
The .afma extension is added automatically when needed.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.cancel.desc:
Cancels the currently running AFMA export job.
Use this if you selected the wrong input or want to change settings before the export finishes.
Temporary export data is discarded when the job is cancelled.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.clear_intro_frame:
Clears the currently selected intro source.
Use this if you want the AFMA to start directly with the main animation instead.
This only clears the input on this screen and does not delete any files.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.close.desc:
Closes the AFMA Creator screen and returns to the previous menu.
If an export job is still running, it is cancelled before the screen closes.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.duplicate_elision:
Skips storing frame payloads for frames that are visually identical to the previous frame.
This is useful for pauses or repeated still frames and usually reduces file size without changing playback.
Disable it only if you specifically want every frame stored separately.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.export.desc:
Starts the AFMA export with the currently selected sources and settings.
Before using this, make sure at least one source is set and the output file path is valid.
The export runs in the background and its progress is shown in the panel above.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.frame_time.desc:
Controls the playback delay of the main animation frames in milliseconds.
Use lower values for faster playback and higher values for slower playback.
Enter a whole number greater than 0.
Controls the playback delay of the optional intro frames in milliseconds.
Use this when the intro should play at a different speed than the main animation.
Enter a whole number greater than 0.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.intro_frames.desc:
Sets an optional intro animation that plays once before the main sequence starts looping.
Type or paste the path to a folder with ordered PNG intro frames, or use the Browse button to choose the directory.
Leave this empty if the animation should start directly with the main sequence.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.keyframe_interval:
Controls how often the encoder stores full reference frames instead of relying on delta-style compression.
Lower values usually improve decoding speed and seeking, while higher values usually reduce file size.
Enter a whole number greater than 0. Changing the optimization preset can overwrite this value.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.loop_count.desc:
Controls how many times the main animation sequence repeats after the intro has finished.
Enter 0 for endless looping. Enter 1 for a single full playthrough, which is basically not looping.
Use 2 or higher for a fixed number of full repeats.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.main_frames.desc:
Sets the main animation source that plays after the optional intro has finished.
Type or paste the path to a folder that contains the ordered PNG frames, or use the Browse button to pick the directory.
You can also drag a folder or ordered PNG files onto this screen.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.max_candidate_axi:
Limits how many major axis-offset motion candidates are tested during rectangle-copy analysis.
Higher values can improve compression on complex motion, but they increase encode-time search work.
Enter a whole number greater than or equal to 0.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.max_copy_search_d:
Limits how far the encoder searches for rectangle-copy matches.
Higher values can find better reuse in large UI movements, but they also make encoding slower.
Enter a whole number greater than or equal to 0.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.near_lossless.des:
Allows a very small visual difference while merging temporal frame data.
This can reduce file size further, but the result is no longer perfectly lossless on a pixel level.
Enable it when smaller files matter more than exact pixel preservation.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.optimization_pres:
Cycles through predefined AFMA encoding profiles.
Click this button to switch between Best Quality, Balanced, and Smallest File.
Changing the preset also updates the keyframe interval and optimization toggles below to match that profile.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.output_file.desc:
Sets the target file path for the exported AFMA archive.
Type or paste the desired output path, or use the Browse button to choose the save location.
If the file name does not end with .afma, the extension is added automatically during export.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.perceptual_alpha_:
Sets the maximum alpha-channel delta allowed for perceptual BIN_INTRA candidates.
Use lower values if transparency edges must stay very stable, or higher values if slightly softer alpha changes are acceptable.
Enter a whole number greater than or equal to 0.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.perceptual_averag:
Sets the maximum average perceptual error allowed for perceptual BIN_INTRA candidates.
Lower values keep the result closer to exact source pixels, while higher values allow stronger palette and shaping optimizations.
Enter a decimal value greater than or equal to 0.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.perceptual_visibl:
Sets the maximum visible color-channel delta allowed for perceptual BIN_INTRA candidates.
Lower values are stricter and keep the result closer to pixel-exact output, while higher values allow more aggressive shrinking.
Enter a whole number greater than or equal to 0.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.rect_copy.desc:
Enables rectangle copy detection during encoding.
When possible, the encoder reuses unchanged rectangular areas from earlier frames instead of storing them again.
This often improves compression, while disabling it can make decoding simpler.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.strict_post_write:
Controls whether the creator reopens the finished AFMA and validates it with the decoder after writing.
Disabled skips that extra roundtrip for much faster exports.
Enable it when you want a stricter export check and do not mind the additional time.
fancymenu.fancymenu.afma.creator.title: AFMA Creator

Fragment shader source code for the Image pass.

- Shadertoy style: void mainImage(out vec4 fragColor, in vec2 fragCoord)
- Direct fragment style: void main()
For multipass setups, use Buffer A-D Source entries.
fancymenu.fancymenu.backgrounds.glsl.mouse_positio: Update iMouse Position Only While Holding LMB: %s

Controls how iMouse.xy is updated when input is enabled.
Enabled: iMouse.xy updates only while the left mouse button is held, then keeps the last held position.
Disabled: iMouse.xy continuously follows cursor movement even when no mouse button is held.
fancymenu.fancymenu.backgrounds.glsl.opacity_multi:
Additional opacity multiplier for this shader background.
Final alpha = background opacity x this multiplier (clamped to 0.0-1.0).
fancymenu.fancymenu.backgrounds.glsl.prefer_inline:
If enabled, FancyMenu tries the shader source first.
If is empty, it falls back to the shader source file.
If disabled, file source is preferred and is only fallback.
fancymenu.fancymenu.backgrounds.glsl.shader_source:
Select a shader source file from local storage, a web URL, or a resource location.
The file must contain plain text GLSL fragment shader code (not binary).
Accepted entry points:
- Shadertoy style: void mainImage(out vec4 fragColor, in vec2 fragCoord)
- Direct fragment style: void main()
In direct mode, output should be written to an out vec4 variable (recommended) or gl_FragColor compatibility.
Supported local file extension: .txt only.
Important: extension is only used for filtering; the content must still be fragment shader code.
fancymenu.fancymenu.backgrounds.glsl.show_compile_:
Shows shader compile/link errors as an overlay on the menu.
Disable if you want to hide diagnostics in production layouts.
fancymenu.fancymenu.backgrounds.glsl.time_scale.de:
Multiplier for shader time progression when not frozen.
1.0 = normal speed, 0.5 = half speed, 2.0 = double speed.
fancymenu.fancymenu.backgrounds.glsl.use_input.des:
If enabled, input-related uniforms are updated from live mouse/keyboard/scroll events.

Auto-sizing will try to adjust the element's size
based on the screen size, so it's never too big or
too small for the current screen size.

Fade-Out will NOT fade-out elements before opening a new menu!

their visibility via loading requirements.

you opened this context menu.

rotation degrees value, but it will also disable rotation grabbers.
fancymenu.fancymenu.element.rotation.degrees.desc:
Set the rotation angle in degrees for this element.
Positive values rotate clockwise.

This is the same as using the grabbers,
but more precise for full control.
fancymenu.fancymenu.element.sticky_anchor.desc:
In this mode, the element's position will get calculated
in a different way than normal.

This mode makes the element always keep the exact same distance
to its anchor, no matter the current size of the element.
This means the size of the element can dynamically change
without it moving away or getting closer to its anchor.
While this can be useful in some situations, there
are also cases where this behaviour is not optimal.

§xThis has NO EFFECT when using another element as anchor!

fancymenu.fancymenu.element.tilt.horizontal.degree:

Positive values tilt the right side away from the viewer.

This is the same as using the grabbers,

fancymenu.fancymenu.element.tilt.vertical.advanced:

fancymenu.fancymenu.elements.button.template_setti:
When you enable the template mode for a custom button, it will apply
some of its settings to all other buttons or sliders in the current screen.

Template buttons will be §linvisible§r outside the editor.

When you set the template to share settings with sliders, the
settings for the button textures will change to slider texture settings.

§lSettings that get shared are:

- Button/Slider Textures
- Button Click Sounds
- Button/Slider Hover Sounds
- Button/Slider Position (if enabled)
- Button/Slider Size (if enabled)
- Button/Slider Opacity (if enabled)
- Button/Slider Visibility (if enabled)

A custom cursor that gets show

fancymenu.fancymenu.elements.cursor.hotspot_x.desc:
The hotspot of a cursor is the
pixel of the cursor texture where
clicks get registered.
For a normal arrow cursor, this
would be the tip of the arrow.

The X0 Y0 coordinate of a texture

fancymenu.fancymenu.elements.cursor.hotspot_y.desc:

The Dragger allows you to make parts of your layout dragable,
which means users can "grab" parts of layouts with

If the drag offset should be persistent
or reset every time the menu gets reopened.

It stays active/visible until the user opens a new screen.

§xONLY FOR ADVANCED USERS!

Allows you to manually set the
position of the element.

Advanced positions support placeholders,
so you can calculate positions
by using the Calculator placeholder,

and much more.

Many useful placeholders for element
positioning can be found

placeholder categories.

Accepted entry points:
- Shadertoy style: void mainImage(out vec4 fragColor, in vec2 fragCoord)
- Direct fragment style: void main()
For multipass setups, use Buffer A-D Source entries.
fancymenu.fancymenu.elements.glsl.mouse_position_r: Update iMouse Position Only While Holding LMB: %s

Controls how iMouse.xy is updated when input is enabled.
Enabled: iMouse.xy updates only while the left mouse button is held, then keeps the last held position.
Disabled: iMouse.xy continuously follows cursor movement even when no mouse button is held.
fancymenu.fancymenu.elements.glsl.opacity_multipli:
Additional opacity multiplier for this shader element.
Final alpha = element opacity x this multiplier (clamped to 0.0-1.0).
fancymenu.fancymenu.elements.glsl.prefer_inline_sh:
If enabled, FancyMenu tries the shader source first.
If is empty, it falls back to the shader source file.
If disabled, file source is preferred and is only fallback.
fancymenu.fancymenu.elements.glsl.shader_source.de:
Select a shader source file from local storage, a web URL, or a resource location.
The file must contain plain text GLSL fragment shader code (not binary).
Accepted entry points:
- Shadertoy style: void mainImage(out vec4 fragColor, in vec2 fragCoord)
- Direct fragment style: void main()
In direct mode, output should be written to an out vec4 variable (recommended) or gl_FragColor compatibility.
Supported local file extension: .txt only.
Important: extension is only used for filtering; the content must still be fragment shader code.
fancymenu.fancymenu.elements.glsl.show_compile_err:

Disable if you want to hide diagnostics in production layouts.
fancymenu.fancymenu.elements.glsl.time_scale.desc:
Multiplier for shader time progression when not frozen.
1.0 = normal speed, 0.5 = half speed, 2.0 = double speed.
fancymenu.fancymenu.elements.glsl.use_input.desc:

fancymenu.fancymenu.listeners.manage.desc:
Listeners are a very powerful feature that allows you to execute an action script when specific things happen, like when a user types on their keyboard, performs a mouse click or even when things happen in worlds, like when the player dies.

Listeners aren't bound to screens, so they constantly listen for events, even if there isn't a screen open at all, like when playing in a singleplayer world or on a server.
fancymenu.fancymenu.listeners.manage.quick_edit_ti: Right-click listeners to quick-edit their actions.
fancymenu.fancymenu.listeners.manage.rename_tip: Rename listeners by double-clicking their display name.
fancymenu.fancymenu.listeners.on_animated_texture_:
This listener triggers when an animated texture (GIF, APNG or FMA) finishes a playback cycle. If the texture loops, it fires right before the animation restarts.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$texture_source §r= The source of the texture (local path, web URL or resource location)
- §z$$texture_source_type §r= Source type (LOCAL, WEB, RESOURCE_LOCATION)
- §z$$texture_will_restart §r= TRUE if the texture will restart after this cycle, otherwise FALSE

This listener triggers when an animated texture (GIF, APNG or FMA) starts playing. It also triggers when the texture restarts because of looping.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$texture_source §r= The source of the texture (local path, web URL or resource location)
- §z$$texture_source_type §r= Source type (LOCAL, WEB, RESOURCE_LOCATION)
- §z$$texture_will_restart §r= TRUE if the texture will restart after this cycle, otherwise FALSE
fancymenu.fancymenu.listeners.on_block_broke.desc:
This listener triggers once when the player breaks a block.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$block_key §r= The resource location of the broken block
- §z$$broke_with_item_key §r= The resource location of the item/tool that was used (or EMPTY when nothing was held)
- §z$$block_pos_x §r= The X coordinate of the broken block
- §z$$block_pos_y §r= The Y coordinate of the broken block
- §z$$block_pos_z §r= The Z coordinate of the broken block
fancymenu.fancymenu.listeners.on_block_placed.desc:

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$block_pos_x §r= The X coordinate of the placed block
- §z$$block_pos_y §r= The Y coordinate of the placed block
- §z$$block_pos_z §r= The Z coordinate of the placed block
fancymenu.fancymenu.listeners.on_char_typed: On Keyboard Character Typed in Screen

Triggers whenever the client displays a normal player chat message.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$chat_message_string §r= Plain text version of the received chat line
- §z$$chat_message_component §r= Full component JSON of the received chat line
- §z$$sender_uuid §r= UUID of the sender (or ERROR if unavailable)
- §z$$sender_name §r= Plain name of the sender (or ERROR if unavailable)
fancymenu.fancymenu.listeners.on_chat_message_sent:

fancymenu.fancymenu.listeners.on_damage_taken.desc:

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$damage_type §r= The resource location of the damage type
- §z$$is_fatal_damage §r= TRUE when the hit reduced the player to zero health
- §z$$damage_source §r= The resource location of the entity that caused the damage or NONE when unavailable
fancymenu.fancymenu.listeners.on_death.desc:

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$death_pos_x §r= X coordinate where the player died
- §z$$death_pos_y §r= Y coordinate where the player died
- §z$$death_pos_z §r= Z coordinate where the player died

fancymenu.fancymenu.listeners.on_enter_structure.d:
§xRequires FancyMenu on the server.§r

This listener triggers once when the player enters a structure using coarse structure-area detection.

Because it considers the entire structure footprint, it can also fire when a structure is near or below the player (for example, a mineshaft beneath the surface).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$structure_key §r= The resource location of the structure the player entered
fancymenu.fancymenu.listeners.on_enter_structure.h:
§xRequires FancyMenu on the server.§r

This listener triggers once when the player actually steps into a structure's interior.

It uses high precision detection, so it only fires when the player enters the structure's bounding boxes.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$structure_key §r= The resource location of the structure the player entered
fancymenu.fancymenu.listeners.on_entity_died.desc:
§xRequires FancyMenu on the server.§r

This listener triggers whenever an entity dies anywhere on the connected server/world (even if the player is far away or in another dimension).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$entity_key §r= The resource location of the entity type that died
- §z$$distance_to_player §r= The distance from the player to the death position (returns -1 when the entity died in another dimension)
- §z$$death_pos_x §r= The X coordinate where the entity died
- §z$$death_pos_y §r= The Y coordinate where the entity died
- §z$$death_pos_z §r= The Z coordinate where the entity died
- §z$$entity_uuid §r= The UUID of the entity that died
- §z$$dimension_key §r= The dimension the entity died in
- §z$$damage_type §r= The resource location of the damage type that caused the death
- §z$$is_same_dimension_as_player §r= If TRUE, the entity died in the same dimension as the player
- §z$$entity_killed_by_name §r= The plain text name of the killer or NONE when unavailable
- §z$$entity_killed_by_key §r= The resource location of the killer's type (uses minecraft:player for players, NONE when unavailable)
- §z$$entity_killed_by_uuid §r= The UUID of the killer or NONE when unavailable
fancymenu.fancymenu.listeners.on_entity_in_sight.d:
This listener triggers once when an entity first becomes visible in the player's field of view (and is not farther away than 200 blocks).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$entity_key §r= The resource location of the visible entity type
- §z$$distance_to_player §r= The distance from the player's eyes to the entity
- §z$$entity_pos_x §r= The entity's X coordinate
- §z$$entity_pos_y §r= The entity's Y coordinate
- §z$$entity_pos_z §r= The entity's Z coordinate
- §z$$entity_uuid §r= The UUID of the visible entity

- §z$$entity_pos_z §r= The entity's Z coordinate when mounting started
- §z$$entity_uuid §r= The UUID of the mounted entity

This listener triggers whenever an entity spawns anywhere on the connected server/world (even if the player is far away or in another dimension).

- §z$$distance_to_player §r= The distance from the player to the spawn location (returns -1 when the entity spawned in another dimension)
- §z$$entity_pos_x §r= The entity's X coordinate at spawn time
- §z$$entity_pos_y §r= The entity's Y coordinate at spawn time
- §z$$entity_pos_z §r= The entity's Z coordinate at spawn time

- §z$$is_same_dimension_as_player §r= If TRUE, the entity spawned in the same dimension as the player

- §z$$entity_pos_x §r= The entity's X coordinate

§xRequires FancyMenu on the server.§r

- §z$$new_value §r= The new variable value
fancymenu.fancymenu.listeners.on_video_playback_st:
This listener triggers whenever video playback state changes.

Possible values for §z$$new_status§r:
- PLAYING: Video started and is now playing (including when resuming from pause)
- STOPPED: Video was stopped through stop()
- PAUSED: Video was paused through pause()
- FINISHED: Video naturally reached the end of playback

If looping is enabled, FINISHED is emitted when the end is reached, right before the next loop starts.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$video_source §r= The source of the video (local path, web URL or resource location)
- §z$$video_source_type §r= Source type (LOCAL, WEB, RESOURCE_LOCATION)
- §z$$is_looping §r= TRUE if looping is enabled, otherwise FALSE
- §z$$new_status §r= New playback status (PLAYING, STOPPED, PAUSED, FINISHED)
fancymenu.fancymenu.listeners.on_weather_changed.d:
This listener triggers once whenever the weather state changes (clear, rain, or thunder).
It will also re-trigger when the local weather changes, which means if it is raining, for example, and you enter a biome that has no rain (desert) or a biome where it is snowing, the listener will re-trigger even though the global weather didn't change.
Entering a building also counts as local weather change while it is raining outside, because well, it doesn't rain inside.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$weather_type §r= The new global weather type (clear, rain, thunder)
- §z$$weather_can_snow §r= TRUE when precipitation at the player renders as snow
- §z$$weather_can_rain §r= TRUE when precipitation at the player renders as rain

- §z$$sound_origin_pos_y §r= The Y position of the sound's origin

If the given number is absolute, the given number is returned.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.absolute_path.des:
Returns the absolute path
of a file/folder.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.alternating_case_:

fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.audio_duration.de:
Returns the total duration of the current track
playing in an Audio element in MM:SS format (e.g. '03:45').
Returns '00:00' if no audio is playing.

Required values:
- element_identifier: The ID of the audio element to get the duration from
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.audio_element_cur:
Gets the filename or display name of the currently playing track in an Audio element.
Returns "---" when no track is playing.
Takes the element identifier of the target Audio element.
Optionally takes display name mappings to show custom names for tracks.
Mapping format: track1.ogg=>Cool Name%%:%%track2.wav=>Another Name
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.audio_element_vol:
Returns the volume of an Audio element
as a value between 0.0 (0%%) and 1.0 (100%%).
Takes the element identifier of the target Audio element.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.audio_playing_sta:
Returns the current playing state of an Audio element.
Use 'element_identifier' to specify the Audio element.
Returns 'true' if the audio is playing, 'false' if paused or stopped.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.audio_playtime.de:
Returns either the current play time of an Audio element
(MM:SS format) or the play progress percentage (0-100).
Returns '00:00' or '0' if no audio is playing.

Required values:
- element_identifier: The ID of the audio element
- show_percentage: Set to 'true' to show percentage instead of time
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.base64_decode.des:
Decodes a Base64 string back to text.

Required values:
- text: The Base64 string to decode
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.base64_encode.des:
Encodes the given text to Base64.

Required values:
- text: The text to encode
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.calc.desc:
Solves arithmetic expressions.

Just replace the example expression
with the real one.

Set 'decimal' to 'false' if the
placeholder should return a LONG
instead of a DOUBLE.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.clicks_per_second:
Returns the clicks per second (CPS) for the given mouse button.

Required values:
- mouse_button: left or right
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.clipboard_content:
Returns the current text content of the system's clipboard
or an empty text if nothing is currently stored in the clipboard.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.crop_text.desc:
Removes a specific amount of characters from the
beginning and end of the given text.

text = The text to crop.
remove_from_start = Characters to remove from the beginning.
remove_from_end = Characters to remove from the end.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.desc:
Add placeholders to the text that later
get replaced with values like the
player name or the Minecraft version.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.element_height.de:
Gets the height of an element
by its element ID.

Just replace 'some.element.id' with
the actual element ID.

§xYou can get the ID of elements
§xby right-clicking them in the editor.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.element_posx.desc:
Gets the X position of an element
by its element ID.

Just replace 'some.element.id' with
the actual element ID.

§xYou can get the ID of elements
§xby right-clicking them in the editor.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.element_posy.desc:
Gets the Y position of an element
by its element ID.

Just replace 'some.element.id' with
the actual element ID.

§xYou can get the ID of elements
§xby right-clicking them in the editor.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.element_width.des:
Gets the width of an element
by its element ID.

Just replace 'some.element.id' with
the actual element ID.

§xYou can get the ID of elements
§xby right-clicking them in the editor.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.error.text_too_lo: §c§lERROR: §rText too long to parse placeholders! 17,000 characters at max!
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.file_md5.desc:
Returns the MD5 hash of a local file.
Only supports local files, not URLs.
Returns an empty string if the file doesn't exist or cannot be read.

You can target the default '.minecraft'
directory by starting the file path with '.minecraft/'.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.file_size.desc:
Returns the size of a local file in bytes.
Only supports local files, not URLs.
Returns 0 if the file doesn't exist or cannot be read.

You can target the default '.minecraft'
directory by starting the file path with '.minecraft/'.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.file_text.desc:
Reads text from a local file or remote URL and returns it.
Supports reading entire content or only the last few lines.

Content is cached to improve performance:
- Local files: Re-read every 1 second
- URLs: Re-read every 10 seconds

Required values:
- path_or_url: The file path or URL to read from
  Local files: Use a path inside the active Minecraft instance (e.g. 'config/myfile.txt')
  Remote files: Use HTTP/HTTPS URLs (e.g. 'https://example.com/data.txt')
  
The file path can start with '.minecraft/' to target the default .minecraft directory. Paths cannot leave either selected root.

Optional values:
- mode: How to read the content (default: 'all')
  Options: 'all' (entire content), 'last' (last X lines)
- separator: Text between lines when joining (default: '\n')
  Common options: '\n' (newline), ' | ', ', ', ' '
- last_lines: Number of lines to return in 'last' mode (default: 1)
  Only used when mode is 'last'

Note: When mode is 'last' with last_lines set to 1,
the single line is returned without any separator.

Returns empty string if source is not cached yet, doesn't exist,
cannot be read, or if there's no internet connection for URLs.

§xSecurity: Imported customizations can use this placeholder to read files inside these roots and combine the result with network actions. Only import customizations you trust, and inspect their placeholders and actions first.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.get_variable.desc:
Gets the text content of a stored variable.
This is only to get variables stored via FancyMenu
and will not work for mod or Vanilla variables.

Just replace 'some_variable' with the actual variable name.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.guiheight.desc: The height of the current screen.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.guiwidth.desc: The width of the current screen.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.json.desc:
Parse JSON and get a value from it.

The 'source' value accepts:
- Direct JSON content (e.g. {"key":"value"})
- Path to a local JSON file inside the active Minecraft instance
- URL to a remote JSON file

Local paths cannot leave the active instance directory. Replace '$.some.json.path' with the JSON path to the value you want to get.

§xSecurity: Imported customizations can use this placeholder to read JSON values inside the instance and combine them with network actions. Only import customizations you trust, and inspect their placeholders and actions first.

§zGo to §ljson.fancymenu.net§r §zto learn more about JSON paths.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.jvm_cpu_usage.des: Gets the current CPU usage of the Java Virtual Machine.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.jvm_name.desc: The name of the Java Virtual Machine.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.kebab_case_text.d:
Converts the input text to kebab-case.

Example:
Input: Hello World
Output: hello-world
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.last_death_messag: Shows the latest death message you received. Set "as_json_component" to true to return the serialized text component instead of plain text.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.last_world_server:
Returns the last world or server the player joined.
You can control via the 'type' value if the placeholder
should return both servers and worlds or only one of them.

Types: both, world, server

The 'full_world_path' value controls if the full path or
only the name of the world (not server) should get returned.
Setting this to 'false' will only return the world name.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.loaded_mods.desc:
Gets the active mods count.
This doesn't include disabled mods.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.loader_name.desc: Gets the name of the mod loader (Forge, Fabric, etc.).
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.loader_version.de: Gets the version of the mod loader (Forge, Fabric, etc.).
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.local.desc:
Localizes a text by the given key.

Just replace 'localization.key' in the
placeholder with a localization key.

Supports Minecraft's localization keys and custom ones!

Check §x§ldocs.fancymenu.net §rfor how to add localizations!
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.lowercase_text.de:
Converts the input text to lowercase letters.

Example:
Input: HELLO WORLD
Output: hello world
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.math_ceil.desc:
Returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to the given number.
For example, ceil(3.14) = 4 and ceil(-3.14) = -3.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.math_cos.desc: Returns the trigonometric cosine of an angle.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.math_cosh.desc: Returns the hyperbolic cosine of a double value.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.math_floor.desc:
Returns the largest integer less than or equal to the given number.
For example, floor(3.14) = 3 and floor(-3.14) = -4.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.math_round.desc:
Rounds a number.
Set the optional 'decimals' value to control the decimal place (use 0 or -1 round to an integer).
Example 1: num=3.14159 & decimals=2 -> 3.14.
Example 2: num=3.14159 & decimals=0 -> 3.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.math_sign.desc:
Returns:
 1 if the number is positive
-1 if the number is negative
 0 if the number is zero
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.math_sin.desc: Returns the trigonometric sine of an angle.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.math_sinh.desc: Returns the hyperbolic sine of a double value.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.math_tan.desc: Returns the trigonometric tangent of an angle.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.math_tanh.desc: Returns the hyperbolic tangent of a double value.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.max_number.desc: Returns the greater of two numbers.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.min_number.desc: Returns the smaller of two numbers.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.minecraft_option_:
Gets the current value of a Minecraft option.
For a list of valid option names, take a look at
the 'options.txt' file of your Minecraft instance.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.modversion.desc:
Gets the version of a mod by its mod ID.

Just replace 'some_mod_id' in the placeholder
with an existing mod ID.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.mouseposx.desc:
Gets the mouse X position.

§xAlways returns 10 while in the editor,
§xso you can still edit the element
§xwithout it following your mouse when
§xusing it for advanced sizing/positioning.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.mouseposy.desc:
Gets the mouse Y position.

§xAlways returns 10 while in the editor,
§xso you can still edit the element
§xwithout it following your mouse when
§xusing it for advanced sizing/positioning.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.nbt_data_get.clie:
Reads NBT directly from the client's world state.
Supports entity selectors with type/name/tag/limit/sort/distance/x/y/z/dx/dy/dz options,
plus absolute or relative block positions, returning value,
string, or SNBT formats entirely client-side.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.nbt_data_get.desc:
Gets NBT data from entities and blocks (similar to '/data get' command).
Returns the value at the specified NBT path.

§lTIP: §rUse the '/data get' command in-game without setting a path
to easily get all available NBT paths for an entity or block!

Required values:
- source_type: The data source type ('entity' or 'block')
- nbt_path: The NBT path to query (e.g. 'foodLevel', 'Pos[0]', 'Inventory[0].id')

Conditional values:
- entity_selector: Entity selector when source_type is 'entity'
  Supports: @s (self), @p (nearest player), @e (nearest entity),
  UUID, or entity name
- block_pos: Block position when source_type is 'block'
  Format: 'x y z' (e.g. '100 64 -200')

Optional values:
- scale: Scale factor for numeric values (default: 1.0)
- return_type: How to return the data (default: 'value')
  Options: 'value' (numeric/size), 'string' (text value),
  'snbt' (formatted NBT), 'json' (JSON format)

Returns empty string if data cannot be accessed or path is invalid.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.nbt_data_get.serv:
§xRequires FancyMenu on the server.§r

Fetches live NBT data from the server, mirroring every target supported by '/data get'.
Returns an empty value until the server response arrives.

The placeholder works exactly like the '/data get' command, so everything that should be possible with the command should also be possible with the placeholder.

Supported source_type values:
- entity: Full selector syntax (scores, advancements, predicates, rotation, gamemode, etc.)
- block: Absolute, relative (~) or local (^) coordinates like the vanilla command
- storage: Command storage identifiers (namespace:key)

Optional arguments:
- nbt_path: Same path rules as '/data get'
- scale: Multiplies numeric results (default 1.0)
- return_type: 'value', 'string', 'snbt', or 'json'

Responses are cached for 100ms to avoid spamming the server.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.negate_number.des:
Returns the negation of the given number.
If the given number is negative, the given number is returned.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.number_base_conve:
Converts a number between bases (supports decimals).
Values: input, from_base (2-36), to_base (2-36).
Up to 16 fractional digits are generated in the target base.
Example: input=67, from_base=10, to_base=2 -> 1000011.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.os.desc: The name of the Operating System.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.os_cpu_usage.desc: Gets the current CPU usage of the Operating System.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.pi.desc: Returns the double value that is closer than any other to §opi§r, the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.random_number.des:
Returns a random number in the specified range.
Returns a different number every tick,
so it's recommended to use the
placeholder in combination with
a variable or something else to
control the refresh rate.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.randomtext.desc:
Picks a random line from a TXT file, URL or direct plain text.

Supports local files, remote URLs and plain text as "source":
- Local files: Use relative paths (e.g. '/config/fancymenu/assets/tips.txt')
- Remote files: Use HTTP/HTTPS URLs (e.g. 'https://example.com/tips.txt')
- Plain text: Input direct plain text. Separate lines with "\n".

Content is automatically reloaded every 30 seconds to pick up changes.

The 'interval' parameter controls how often a new random line is selected
from the loaded content (in seconds).

An interval of 0 will make it pick a line only once per session.

For local files, just replace '<file_name.txt>' with your file path.
Local files HAVE to be placed in FancyMenu's ASSETS folder!
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.realtime_day.desc:
Returns the current real-world day of the month.

Values:
- timezone: Timezone to use for this placeholder. Defaults to 'system'. It is recommended to use IANA timezone IDs here. A good website to see all IANA IDs is https://nodatime.org/TimeZones
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.realtime_hour.des:
Returns the current real-world hour.
Defaults to 24-hour format (00-23).

Values:
- twelve_hour_format: Set to 'true' to return 12-hour format instead (01-12)
- timezone: Timezone to use for this placeholder. Defaults to 'system'. It is recommended to use IANA timezone IDs here. A good website to see all IANA IDs is https://nodatime.org/TimeZones
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.realtime_minute.d:
Returns the current real-world minute.

Values:
- timezone: Timezone to use for this placeholder. Defaults to 'system'. It is recommended to use IANA timezone IDs here. A good website to see all IANA IDs is https://nodatime.org/TimeZones
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.realtime_month.de:
Returns the current real-world month.

Values:
- timezone: Timezone to use for this placeholder. Defaults to 'system'. It is recommended to use IANA timezone IDs here. A good website to see all IANA IDs is https://nodatime.org/TimeZones
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.realtime_second.d:
Returns the current real-world second.

Values:
- timezone: Timezone to use for this placeholder. Defaults to 'system'. It is recommended to use IANA timezone IDs here. A good website to see all IANA IDs is https://nodatime.org/TimeZones
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.realtime_year.des:
Returns the current real-world year.

Values:
- timezone: Timezone to use for this placeholder. Defaults to 'system'. It is recommended to use IANA timezone IDs here. A good website to see all IANA IDs is https://nodatime.org/TimeZones
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.replace_text.desc:
Replaces text in a string using either literal text or regular expressions (regex).
Supports both single replacement and replace-all operations.

Required values:
- text: The input text to perform replacements on
- search: The text or regex pattern to search for

Optional values:
- replacement: The replacement text (default: empty string)
- use_regex: Set to 'true' to use regex patterns (default: 'false')
- replace_all: Set to 'true' to replace all occurrences, otherwise only first occurrence (default: 'true')

When using regex, you can use capture groups like $1, $2, etc.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.screen_identifier: Returns the identifier of the screen that is currently open. Returns an empty value if no screen is open.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.sentence_case_tex:
Converts the input text to sentence case.

Example:
Input: hello world. this is fancymenu!
Output: Hello world. This is fancymenu!
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.servermotd.desc:
Gets the MOTD of a server.
Just replace 'someserver.com:25565'
with the actual server IP
and '1' with the MOTD line.
MOTDs only have 2 lines, so
the only valid line values are
'1' and '2'.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.serverping.desc:
Gets the ping to a server.

Just replace 'someserver.com:25565' in the
placeholder with a valid server IP.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.serverplayercount:
Gets the player count of a server.

Just replace 'someserver.com:25565' in the
placeholder with a valid server IP.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.serverstatus.desc:
Gets the status (online/offline) of a server.

Just replace 'someserver.com:25565' in the
placeholder with a valid server IP.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.serverversion.des:
Gets the MC version of a server.

Just replace 'someserver.com:25565' in the
placeholder with a valid server IP.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.snake_case_text.d:
Converts the input text to snake_case.

Example:
Input: Hello World
Output: hello_world
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.split_text.desc:
Splits a text at a specific character or regex.

input = The text to split.
regex = The character or regex for where to split the text.
max_parts = The max parts the text should get split into. Setting this to -1 disables the limit.
split_index = The part that should get returned after splitting. Starts at 0.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.stringify.desc:
Stringifies a text by escaping all
syntax characters ( " { } ).

This is useful when nesting other
placeholders as value. If the
replaced nested placeholder could
contain syntax characters that aren't
part of another placeholder, you need
to escape them.

§xPlaceholders in the value will be
§xreplaced first, so you don't need
§xto worry about them getting stringified.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.switch_case.desc:
Matches a value against multiple cases and returns the corresponding result.
Format: value to match, case pairs (value:result) separated by commas, optional default case.
Example: value="1", cases="1:first,2:second", default="none"
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.text_char_count.d: Returns the character count of the given text.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.text_input_field_:
Returns the current value of an input field (text box) by its element identifier.
Works for custom and Vanilla elements.
Returns an empty value if the element was not found or is not an input field.

Required values:
- element_identifier: The element identifier of the target element
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.text_width.desc:
Returns the width in pixels of the given text.
Useful for calculating element positions or sizes based on text width.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.title_case_text.d:
Converts the input text to Title Case.

Example:
Input: hello world
Output: Hello World
Toggles the case of each letter in the input text.

Example:
Input: Toggle Case
Output: tOGGLE cASE
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.totalmods.desc:
Gets the total mods count.
This includes disabled mods.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.trim_text.desc:
Removes all leading and trailing spaces of the
given text, but not spaces within the text.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.unix_time.desc:
The current time in milliseconds, measured by the time
that has elapsed since 00:00:00 UTC on 1 January 1970.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.uppercase_text.de:
Converts the input text to uppercase letters.

Example:
Input: Hello World
Output: HELLO WORLD
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.uptime_seconds.de: Returns the time since the game launched in seconds or, if "output_as_millis" is true, in milliseconds.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.vanillabuttonlabe:
Get the label/text of a Vanilla widget/button.

Replace 'some.menu.identifier:505280' with
the correct widget locator
of the target widget.

The widget locator points to a specific
widget in a specific screen.

§xYou can right-click widgets
§xin the editor to copy their locator.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.video_background_:
Returns the total duration of a Video menu background in MM:SS format (e.g. '03:45') or in milliseconds by its identifier.
Returns '00:00' or '0' if the background is not ready yet or no video is set.

Required values:
- background_identifier: The ID of the Video background
- output_as_timestamp: Set to 'true' to show milliseconds instead of MM:SS

To get the identifier of a background, right-click the
editor background and click on 'Copy Background Identifier'.

Returns the paused state of a Video menu background by its identifier.
Returns 'true' when the element is paused, otherwise returns 'false'.

To get the identifier of a background, right-click the
editor background and click on 'Copy Background Identifier'.

Returns either the current play time of a Video menu background
(MM:SS format), the play progress percentage (0-100), or the current play time in milliseconds.
Returns '00:00' or '0' if the element is not ready yet or no video is set.

Required values:
- background_identifier: The ID of the Video background
- show_percentage: Set to 'true' to show percentage instead of time
- output_as_timestamp: Set to 'true' to show milliseconds instead of MM:SS

Priority:
- show_percentage (highest)
- output_as_timestamp
- default MM:SS output

To get the identifier of a background, right-click the
editor background and click on 'Copy Background Identifier'.

Returns the volume of a Video menu background by its identifier.
The volume is a decimal between 0.0 (0%%) and 1.0 (100%%).

To get the identifier of a background, right-click the
editor background and click on 'Copy Background Identifier'.
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.video_element_dur:
Returns the total duration of a Video element in MM:SS format (e.g. '03:45') or in milliseconds.
Returns '00:00' or '0' if the element is not ready yet or no video is set.

Required values:
- element_identifier: The ID of the Video element to get the duration from
- output_as_timestamp: Set to 'true' to show milliseconds instead of MM:SS
fancymenu.fancymenu.placeholders.video_element_pla:
Returns either the current play time of a Video element
(MM:SS format), the play progress percentage (0-100), or the current play time in milliseconds.
Returns '00:00' or '0' if the element is not ready yet or no video is set.

Required values:
- element_identifier: The ID of the Video element
- show_percentage: Set to 'true' to show percentage instead of time
- output_as_timestamp: Set to 'true' to show milliseconds instead of MM:SS

Priority:
- show_percentage (highest)
